mainEntity.name: How Often Does a Dry Conveyor System Need to Be Cleaned?

acceptedAnswer.text: The plant's sanitation program sets the routine. Dry zones for industrialized foods typically see moderate, infrequent cleaning by vacuum, brushing and wipe-down, with water kept out of the area. TRFCleanflow Dry is designed for dry and low-moisture environments where cleanability is required.

mainEntity.name: Which Food Plants Use a Dry Conveyor System?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dry and low-moisture zones exist in many food plants, including the priority industries of TRFCleanflow: frozen food, dairy and cheese, ready-to-eat and food processing, and protein processing plants with dry packaging areas. Your sanitation team defines each zone, and TRF designs the conveyor to match it.

mainEntity.name: Can a Dry Conveyor System Connect to Packaging and Case Packing Equipment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFCleanflow Dry is engineered to connect processing, inspection and primary packaging with the downstream automation, so start, stop and product flow are coordinated across the line. After primary packaging, TRFIntraflow carries the packed product to case packing and palletizing, and one partner defines every interface in the same project.
